chapter: New York choir and Rae Harrison
title: Back in Philadelphia, the choir with band effects, and Lud Gluskin
summary: He returns to Philadelphia, builds a choir with band-like effects, never records, and mentions his friend Lud Gluskin at CBS.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: See, so that's the way that happened. So it was just one of those things. That we had to go back. So we came back here. And when I came back to America, let's see, well, I went back to Philadelphia, because my mother was just living. She died in the next month or something like that. But I was staying with my brother. He's a doctor in Philadelphia, see. And we stayed there. And then I made up my mind what I wanted to do. And I took the choir, see?
But now, this choir was unique. Because I gave the choir the same effects that I'd give a band.
And actually one man called it sing-music.
You never made any records? You never recorded that choir, huh?
No. I couldn't get the -- a friend of mine, Lud Gluskin. He's out there in Hollywood, you know, he had that CBS with Hollywood, Lud Gluskin.

Well, Lud Gluskin, he was just a little (E-flat) drummer when -- and a leader, when we was in Berlin, you know? And I -- right now, if I was writing to Lud Gluskin, if he's still in the business, he'd try to do something for me, came here and went in with CBS, you know? But of course, he (unintelligible). I guess he had his relatives or something, put him in. And he went on for years. He was head of the music department out in Hollywood, CBS.
